einzeiler: Poet Mark Wunderlich discusses Spencer Reese and reads his own work.
kurzfassung: Poet Mark Wunderlich joins Kevin Young to discuss and analyze the poem My Great Grandmother's Bible by Spencer Reese. They explore the sonnet's intricate rhyme scheme, themes of family inheritance, and connections to the AIDS Memorial Quilt. Later, Wunderlich reads his own poem The Bats and reflects on writing during the pandemic and living in a historic home.
stichpunkte: Mark Wunderlich selects My Great Grandmother's Bible by Spencer Reese from the New Yorker archive
Discussion of the sonnet as a linguistic machine and the emotional resonance of its tight internal rhymes
Connecting the domestic imagery of family Bibles and sewing to the Names Project AIDS Memorial Quilt
The intersections of religious language, poetic tradition, and queer history in Reese's work
Mark Wunderlich reads his New Yorker-published poem The Bats
Exploration of how the constraints of rhyme create momentum and surprise during composition
Reflecting on pandemic isolation, insomnia, and the atmosphere of a centuries-old home
Wunderlich discusses his upcoming book Mady and its unexpected historical inspirations

clips.hook: The largest collective folk art project ever created
clips.text: The AIDS Memorial Quilt stands as the biggest collaborative folk art initiative globally, featuring tens of thousands of panels dedicated to individuals lost to the epidemic.

clips.hook: When funeral homes turned away victims of a crisis
clips.text: During the height of the AIDS crisis in the 1980s and 1990s, numerous individuals faced social abandonment and were denied basic burial rites and funeral services.

clips.hook: Rhyme as an engine that drives a poem forward
clips.text: Starting to incorporate rhyme introduces a distinct momentum into the writing process, functioning much like turning on a car motor.

clips.hook: A three-hundred-year-old dwelling that resembles a face
clips.text: The historic Dutch house features architectural details on the roof peak that give the exterior structure the distinct appearance of a human head.

clips.hook: Historic French terminology describing agreements among pirates
clips.text: Scholars view a specific historical term for pirate alliances as an early precursor to same-sex marriage, where crew members established legal pacts to share resources and protect each other.

beschreibung:
Mark Wunderlich joins Kevin Young to read and discuss “My Great-Grandmother’s Bible,” by Spencer Reece, and his own poem “The Bats.” Wunderlich is the author of five books of poems, including “The Anchorage,” which received the Lambda Literary Award; “The Earth Avails,” which won the Rilke Prize; and “God of Nothingness,” which was published in 2021. His new book, “MATEY,” is forthcoming from Graywolf Press.
